research.summary: Second-generation hardware, ironmongery, tools and plumbing supplies shop at 147–149 Tottenham Lane, Hornsey N8, incorporated 20 May 1977 — 49 years trading, one employee. Reviewers call it an "Aladdin's Cave" and praise the staff for patiently walking non-trade customers through DIY jobs step by step; one review reads "priceless but pricey". A neighbour posted in the Hornsey Village Life Facebook group: "I am always amazed at how many people don't know about Patel's. Best tool shop in North London" — seven comments followed, including one about "the added entertainment of watching the owners bicker". Sanji Karsan Patel (56) has been director since 1995 and holds 75%+ of shares — he is the buyer and almost certainly the man who answers the phone. Irene Margaret Patel (83) is also a director; founder Karsan Harji Patel resigned in 2009. The honest problem: cash at bank is £1,912, down from £8,541 the year before, with £69,674 of reserves mostly tied up in stock. £400 is roughly a fortnight's cash for this business — the digital opportunity is real and the goodwill is real, but affordability is a genuine constraint, not a negotiating position.

Lead with the free Google category fix and the Facebook quote. If he says he can't afford it, believe him immediately, fix the category anyway, and leave the door open. A 49-year-old family shop that remembers you being decent is worth more later than a sale squeezed today.
Best time to call: mid-morning. They open 08:30 and close 17:00, a narrower window than most other prospects — this is genuinely the only realistic slot.
Read the Facebook quote to him directly, don't editorialise it. It's a neighbour's words, not yours, and it does all the work on its own.

Honest odds from the research: 9/10 chance of getting through (one employee, he'll answer), 5/10 of booking a meeting (the Facebook hook genuinely lands), but only 2/10 of closing — not because he doesn't want it, because of the cash position.

Never mention the £75/month or £50/month products on this call — everything here is genuinely true of what he doesn't need yet, and saying so plainly is the most credible thing you can do on this particular call.

Irene Margaret Patel (83) is also a director; founder Karsan Harji Patel resigned in 2009 — this is a second-generation shop, and the Facebook comment about "the owners bickering" is presumably part of the charm, not a red flag.

script.opening: Morning — is {{firstName}} about? ... You don't know me, and I'll be straight with you — this is a cold call. Thirty seconds, and if it's no use I'll go away.
script.hook: Someone posted in the Hornsey Village Life Facebook group the other week — said they're always amazed how many people don't know about Patel's, best tool shop in North London. Seven people replied. That's not me saying it, that's a neighbour.
script.valueStatement: What I do is small and specific. One page: what you stock, your hours, that Facebook post and your other reviews on it, and your name pointing at you instead of nobody finding you at all. That's it — nothing you don't need.
script.demoOffer: Here's what I'd suggest. Separate from all that — Google's got you down as a hardware shop, not a plumbers' merchant. I'll get that corrected for you, no charge, whether you want anything else or not. If it ever suits, I could also put together what a page might look like — no pressure at all, and no cost to you just to see it.
script.pricing: It's four hundred pounds, once. If that's not right for you at the moment, that's a completely genuine reason and I'm not going to push it — the category fix is happening either way.
